thread:
Sophie: Quick sync — after quantized bring-up (ggml/q8), runner metrics jump ~2-4% across runs. Suspect KV cache staleness or fixture regen. @Miguel @Anya any ideas?
Miguel: Have you tried kicking the KV cache? `runner.flush_kv_cache()` before each eval batch helps in local tests.
Sophie: I did a few runs with flush, variance dropped but not gone. Also saw some fixtures re-generated in CI logs: `fixtures/2024-11-07/*` which is suspicious.
Anya: Hmm, we've had that before — CI sometimes regenerates synthetic fixtures when SEED isn't pinned. The script `ci/evals/regenerate.py` falls back to time seed when env var missing.
Sophie: oh yikes. log excerpt:
```
INFO: regenerating fixture for cohort A
SEED is not set, using seed=1700000001
```
Miguel: That would create different prompts and change metric distribution. We should gate against fixture drift.
Raj: CI also showed checksum mismatch on shard 42 yesterday:
`shard-42.checksum: a3f5.. vs a3f6..`
Raj: I'll paste the failing shard diff after lunch.
eval-bot: Eval-run 1893449000 finished. metric: accuracy=0.814 +- 0.022 across 5 runs. note: variant=ggml-q8
Sophie: Proposal: add two CI guards — 1) fixture checksum assert on PR (fail if new checksum unless flagged), 2) env SEED required for regen jobs. Also run a nightly job that compares quantized baseline vs fp32 on canonical promptset.
devex: I can add a lightweight GitHub Action that checks fixture checksums against S3. Should we store canonical checksums in `s3://redwood-eval/canonical/`?
Miguel: Yes. Also add explicit metric tag `baseline:fp32` and `baseline:ggml-q8` so dashboards don't conflate them.
ci-bot: scheduled job created: `ci/check-fixture-checksum` (cron: daily)
Anya: And we should mark the regen script to fail loudly if SEED unset. Patch incoming from me.
Sophie: Thanks — next steps: Raj posts shard diff, Devex wires action, Anya PR, I'll update dashboard labels. If we still see >1% variance after this, we'll dig into kernel nondeterminism.
Miguel: Also log RNG state at warmup boundaries, helps triage.
Sophie: agree. :thumbsup:
